business.title: A MATLAB-based AI-IoT simulation framework for LSTM-driven smart solar irrigation and renewable energy management
business.description: Smart irrigation offers a great avenue for better water use efficiency, and farming sustainability. However, most of the studies conducted so far tend to concentrate on the monitoring systems and platforms of the Internet of Things (IoT) or on the prediction models based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) (but not on both). To address this gap, this research study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Internet of Things (IoT) system to predict the water consumption requirements and control the energy produced by a PV system along with a battery State of Charge (SOC) management system, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, adaptive pump-speed control, and conceptual IoT communication architecture. A dataset of real environmental data from the NASA POWER database was used to test the framework for Egypt’s New Delta region. The LSTM model was able to classify the irrigation pump operating states with an accuracy of 96.11%, a recall of 0.9820, a precision of 0.9100, and an F1-score of 0.9446. It had a better performance than the two models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) when compared and robustness testing with various independent training runs showed a stable performance in predicting. An estimated annual water-saving rate of 28.57% was obtained relative to the assumed conventional fixed-schedule baseline, while motor energy use was reduced by 74.74% through adaptive pump-speed control. A sensitivity analysis was also performed, showing that the model was stable to moderate variations in environmental and operating conditions. Combined, these findings suggest that the use of AI-based modelling for renewable energy management in the context of an irrigation simulation model built in MATLAB could be a valuable asset in improving irrigation efficiency and lowering water and energy use, which is a promising start for future implementation of hardware versions of intelligent, solar-powered irrigation devices.

science.title: A Groundbreaking Milestone in Mathematical Research
science.description: In the evolving landscape of mathematical verification, the exclusive human-held authority to deliver final adjudication over rigorous mathematical proofs is progressively transferring to advanced computing machines. This paradigm shift redefines traditional scholarly validation workflows, leveraging automated proof assistants and formal verification systems to eliminate human-induced logical gaps, resolve long-standing mathematical conjectures, and establish unprecedentedly rigorous, reproducible benchmarks for certifying the validity of complex mathematical derivations. As formal verification technologies mature, the transfer of this core adjudicative power reshapes the foundational norms of mathematical research, opening new frontiers for cross-disciplinary collaboration between mathematicians and computer scientists while sparking critical discussions about the evolving boundaries of human cognitive authority in formal scientific validation.

science.title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
science.description: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe48Mn32Co10Cr10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation. Nanosized multi-principal element alloy single-crystals achieve both strength ~3 GPa and uniform elongation ~20% due to uneven enthalpy distribution, which promotes random, widespread defect formation and prevents localized stress buildup.

science.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
science.description: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response. Glycosylation is critical for an effective immune response, but immune cell glycan dynamics are not fully understood. Here, the authors present GlycoStamp-seq to track sialoglycan dynamics, and apply GlycoStamp-seq in an oxaliplatin-treated subcutaneous bladder cancer mouse model.

science.title: A hybrid deep learning and circuit-theoretic framework for module-level fault diagnosis and localization in pv arrays
science.description: The rapid global expansion of photovoltaic (PV) systems necessitates robust fault management for minimizing operational downtime and enhancing system reliability under fluctuating environmental conditions. Current diagnostic methodologies, however, often lack the necessary robustness and generalizability to data-driven scenarios or to differentiate sub-string faults under dynamic partial shading conditions (PSCs) and realistic irradiance gradients. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid diagnostic framework that is evaluated under non-ideal operating conditions, specifically accounting for realistic cable and busbar resistances. The proposed pipeline decouples discrete topological classification from continuous physics-based estimation. In the first stage, a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-Attention architecture classifies the topology, resolving ambiguities in electrical profiles at critical healthy-to-PSC boundaries with 99.76% classification accuracy. Subsequently, the identified topology is fed into a deterministic circuit-analysis framework to perform module-level fault localization. The proposed non-iterative mathematical core directly maps terminal metrics ($$\:{V}_{i}^{cal}$$, V1PVi, Ii and IEndi) to physical fault location, achieving a discrimination accuracy of 100% for variable-resistance line-to-ground (LG) faults and 100% for zero-resistance line-to-line (ILL) faults within solid intra-string bypass configurations. Furthermore, due to the analytical nature of the localization equations, the proposed technique remains invariant to fluctuations in irradiance and temperature, provided these environmental parameters are uniform across the PV array. Simulation results on a 3 × 5 PV array confirm that the proposed approach sustains high diagnostic accuracy even under measurement noise and parameter uncertainty, demonstrating its promise as a robust diagnostic method for PV arrays.
